findings.summary: The login experience ignores the user’s dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical to the light screenshot; the probe reports color-scheme "normal" and a white body background while prefers-color-scheme: dark matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define semantic surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), preserving SBI brand contrast.

findings.summary: State and route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM and CSS probe found no authored view-transition rules or calls; attempted Open Now navigation remained on the welcome state without a visual continuity cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Use document.startViewTransition for same-document state changes and @view-transition for eligible cross-document routes, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Long content has no position-aware navigation or progress affordance.
findings.evidence: The privacy page is 9,307 CSS pixels tall at 360px, while its screenshot and DOM show only a static logo header and no progress, section navigation, or scroll-state response.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading-progress or section affordance using scroll-state/container queries, and keep it non-obstructive.

findings.summary: Components adapt only at page/viewport level, not at their container boundary.
findings.evidence: The CSSOM probe found zero @container rules across the loaded application despite the login and content-card components being reused in materially different widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable shells an inline-size container and move component-specific breakpoints to @container queries with a viewport-query fallback.

findings.summary: Several primary links and text-size controls have undersized hit areas.
findings.evidence: The rendered target probe measured Get Help and WhatsApp at 14px high, footer and recovery links at 16–21px high, and A-/A/A+ controls only 9–17px wide.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand interactive hit areas to at least 24×24 CSS pixels, preferably 44×44 on touch layouts, without reducing visible spacing.

findings.summary: The prominent Open Now account-opening path does not reach its advertised journey.
findings.evidence: Direct navigation to the linked savings-account landing URL returned to /registration/welcome, and an attempted Open Now activation remained on the welcome URL and state.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore the public account-opening route, use a real navigable href, preserve deep-link routing, and show an actionable error if onboarding is unavailable.

findings.summary: Submitting the empty login state provides no visible or programmatic recovery feedback.
findings.evidence: After activating Login with all fields empty, the page text was unchanged, :invalid returned no controls, and the four aria-live regions remained empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply native constraints, validate after interaction, place specific messages beside each field, set aria-invalid, and announce an error summary through a populated live region.

findings.summary: The primary banking entry page is slow to become useful.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 12.3s, FCP 6.3s, TBT 670ms and a performance score of 0.38; the independent trace measured FCP/LCP 5.08s and TBT 182.68ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content, eliminate the redirect where possible, reduce boot-time JavaScript, and defer non-critical analytics and application features.

findings.summary: Large, mostly unused JavaScript blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 575KiB of unused JavaScript, 2.1s JavaScript execution, a 650ms maximum potential FID, and 670ms TBT; the trace recorded a 232.68ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the long task, split route code, tree-shake unused dependencies, and schedule non-critical work after the core login UI is interactive.

findings.summary: The load has an expensive redirect and an oversized dependency chain.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 131 requests and 1.91MB transferred, including 37 scripts/1.31MB and 216KB fonts; Lighthouse estimated 1.27s redirect savings and found a font-display delay.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the canonical entry directly, preload only true critical dependencies, subset/swap fonts, and defer non-essential chunks and third parties.

findings.summary: Heading hierarchy is not logical on key pages.
findings.evidence: The privacy page jumps from one H1 to eleven H6 headings and Lighthouse failed heading-order; the welcome page uses three H1 elements plus empty H2/H5/H6 elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one page H1 and sequential H2/H3 section headings; remove empty headings and use CSS, not heading rank, for visual sizing.

findings.summary: The mobile privacy policy is needlessly narrow and laborious to read.
findings.evidence: At 360px the text is confined to an approximately 209px-wide inset card, causing the page to extend to 9,307px and forcing excessive wrapping.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce mobile card insets, set a comfortable measure using ch units at larger sizes, and let the content use most of the small viewport.

findings.summary: Three security-practice images are distorted.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified three carousel images rendered around 0.67 aspect ratio although their natural ratios are 1.01–1.14.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve intrinsic aspect ratio with width/height or aspect-ratio and object-fit, and avoid forcing all editorial images into one distorted box.

findings.summary: The app carries deprecated and navigation-hostile platform behavior.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found a deprecated unload listener in polyfills, an IndexedDB event preventing BFCache restoration, and missing source maps for three large first-party bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload handlers, close or avoid IndexedDB work around pagehide/freeze, verify BFCache restoration, and publish protected production source maps.

findings.summary: Public pages have generic titles and no meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: Both welcome and privacy routes use the same title “YONO SBI”; DOM and Lighthouse found no meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every public route a unique descriptive title and concise description, for example “YONO SBI Net Banking Login | State Bank of India”.

findings.summary: The public entry page is effectively empty to non-JavaScript crawlers and many links are not crawlable.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 1% raw/rendered content coverage and isJsShell=true; crawler screenshot is blank. Lighthouse found 20 anchors without valid destinations and robots.txt returned application HTML with 17 parse errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render public content and navigation, emit real href destinations, and serve a valid text/plain robots.txt and sitemap instead of the SPA shell.

findings.summary: Canonical, sitemap, and share/entity metadata are absent or invalid.
findings.evidence: DOM probes found no canonical, Open Graph, or structured metadata; sitemap.xml returned the same 89KB Angular shell rather than a sitemap, and the entry performs a 307 cross-host redirect.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose one canonical public host, emit per-route canonical and social metadata plus Organization/WebSite JSON-LD, and publish a valid XML sitemap consistent with robots policy.

findings.summary: A banking entry page sets an insecure cookie and weakens its CSP.
findings.evidence: The cookies audit found TLTSID without Secure or HttpOnly and with SameSite=None; CSP allows unsafe-inline for script and style. HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and X-Frame-Options are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure, HttpOnly and an appropriate Lax/Strict SameSite value; migrate inline scripts/styles to nonces or hashes and tighten CSP after report-only validation.

findings.summary: Tracking and background calls are neither minimal nor accurately disclosed.
findings.evidence: Trackers found Google Tag Manager plus Firebase services; HAR recorded 130 cross-origin requests relative to the requested host and gtag requests with id=undefined. The privacy page states “We do not use cookies” although TLTSID is set.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory and purpose-limit telemetry, remove malformed/unused GTM, gate non-essential analytics on informed choice, and update the privacy statement to match actual cookies and processors.

findings.summary: The page requests location on load and exposes only password authentication.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed geolocation-on-start at polyfills code; the sign-in DOM exposes username/password with no WebAuthn/passkey affordance and the password field lacks current-password autocomplete.
findings.suggestedFix: Request location only after a clear user gesture and purpose explanation; add passkey sign-in/registration while retaining a secure recovery path and correct autocomplete tokens.

findings.summary: The public content and navigation disappear without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML contains only one content token while the rendered page contains 139; discoverability reports 1% coverage and the no-JS crawler screenshot is blank.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the login guidance, notices, help links and public information; layer client behavior on semantic forms and links rather than an empty Angular root.

findings.summary: The app-like banking experience has no installability or explicit offline fallback metadata.
findings.evidence: DOM probes found no web app manifest. The browser supports service workers, but no install surface or captured offline fallback was exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a minimal manifest and service-worker-controlled offline shell that clearly explains unavailable online banking actions and offers safe retry/help paths.

findings.summary: A linked legal route can fail as a generic 403 with no recovery.
findings.evidence: During the representative direct-route capture, Terms of Service displayed only “403 ERROR – The request could not be satisfied,” without SBI navigation, retry, contact, or return actions; later HEAD requests were intermittent, reinforcing the need for robust handling.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix edge routing/cache consistency and replace generic edge failures with a branded, accessible recovery response containing retry, home, and support actions.

findings.summary: The privacy statement contradicts observed site behavior.
findings.evidence: The visible policy says “We do not use cookies on our web site,” while CDP observed TLTSID and the page loads GTM and Firebase services.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish an accurate, plain-language inventory of essential and non-essential cookies and processors, including purpose, retention, choice, and deletion controls.

findings.summary: The sign-in form disables or omits standard password-manager assistance.
findings.evidence: Username uses autocomplete=off and the password field has no autocomplete token; fields have no stable names in the rendered form probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Use stable name/id values with autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password; retain paste support and let password managers fill the form.

findings.summary: The advertised new-account action is not a dependable, transparent account flow.
findings.evidence: Open Now advertises account creation, but both activation evidence and direct routing failed to leave the welcome page, with no explanation or alternative.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the route dependable, explain eligibility and required steps before collecting data, and preserve a clear cancel/back/support path throughout onboarding.

findings.summary: The entry route transfers and executes substantial work with little immediate value.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 1.91MB/131 requests; Lighthouse estimated 575KiB unused JavaScript and 40KiB unused CSS, while malformed GTM id=undefined requests and multiple Firebase calls occur before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-level byte/request budget, remove malformed analytics, lazy-load non-login modules and below-fold media, and eliminate unused CSS/JavaScript.

findings.summary: Login validation does not help the user understand or correct omissions.
findings.evidence: Activating Login on empty fields produced no visible message, no native invalid controls and no populated alert/live region.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate on submit/blur after interaction, identify each missing field in plain language, focus an error summary, and preserve entered values.

findings.summary: Reflow works, but touch target sizing does not meet an inclusive baseline.
findings.evidence: Mobile layouts had zero horizontal overflow, but the target-size probe found many visible actions only 14–21px high and text-size controls as narrow as 9px.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain the successful reflow while expanding all interactive target boxes and spacing adjacent controls to prevent accidental activation.
